summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Question: what run-of-river output variability is projected under climate scenarios. PENDING: no projection or observation retrieved. Leads: ICIMOD basin-scale hydropower risk work, glacial lake inventory and the 2026 Kyirong-Rasuwa flood account (all located by 16A search), NEA annual reports for observed generation by plant; IPCC AR6 WGII (Ch.10, CCP5), IPCC SROCC Ch.2, ICIMOD HIMAP 2019 and a peer-reviewed runoff projection study are recorded as general-knowledge URLs to be verified on fetch because the r1 web-search budget was exhausted before 22D searches. Method designed: translate projected changes in basin runoff (annual total, monsoon vs dry-season flow, low-flow percentiles, timing of peak water) into run-of-river generation using observed flow-generation relationships per plant (DHM discharge + NEA generation), separately for snow/glacier-fed and rain-fed basins, near term (to mid-century) and late century, and under at least two emission scenarios. Hazard exposure (GLOF, debris flows, sediment) is reported as a separate outage/damage channel, not mixed into flow variability.

findings.claim: Projected change in annual and seasonal (monsoon, dry-season) runoff for Nepal's main basins (Koshi, Gandaki, Karnali, Mahakali) by period and emission scenario.
findings.note: HIMAP 2019 / HI-WISE 2023 chapters, IPCC AR6 WGII Ch.10 and CCP5, basin studies; record each model ensemble range with scenario (RCP/SSP), baseline period and projection period.

findings.claim: Projected change in dry-season low flows and in inter-annual variability (e.g. coefficient of variation of annual flow), which drive run-of-river firm energy.
findings.note: Basin-scale ICIMOD studies; DHM station records for baseline variability.

findings.claim: Timing of 'peak water' from glacier melt in Nepal's basins and implication for dry-season flow after the peak.
findings.note: HIMAP, SROCC Ch.2, AR6 CCP5; academic studies (e.g. lead L08).

findings.claim: Observed inter-annual and seasonal variability of run-of-river generation (NEA plants), FY2010/11 onward.
findings.note: NEA annual reports monthly generation by plant; compute monsoon/dry ratio and year-to-year variation per plant and system.

findings.claim: Share of generation capacity in snow/glacier-fed basins (links to 16B EXP-07, owned by 25A).
findings.note: NEA plant list by river + ICIMOD basin melt-contribution; threshold to be set by 25A as labelled assumption.

findings.claim: Climate-related hazard outages: GLOF/debris-flow/sediment events affecting hydropower (including the August 2026 Kyirong-Rasuwa event).
findings.note: ICIMOD event account (lead L03), BIPAD portal; record as dated events with plants affected and outage duration - separate from flow variability.

findings.claim: Run-of-river output variability is modelled as generation = f(flow) per plant with capacity and minimum environmental flow constraints; projections of flow are not converted into generation without plant-level observed relationships.
Projection ranges from different studies (ICIMOD, IPCC-assessed literature, individual papers) are reported separately with scenario, model ensemble and baseline period; they are not averaged.

data_gaps: All projection and observation values - no document downloaded in r1.

Web-search budget exhausted before 22D-specific searches; leads L04-L09 are general-knowledge URLs flagged for verification on fetch; HI-WISE 2023 and basin-specific studies still need exact document URLs.
DHM station discharge series may require a formal data request rather than download.
Plant-level hydrological design data (design discharge, flow-duration curves) from DoED/NEA not located.
World Bank Nepal CCDR (climate and development report) hydropower chapter not located.
No unit code for discharge (m3/s) or for runoff depth (mm) in units.py; percent change will be used where possible.

assumptions.text: Variability is reported as ranges (min-max across models/scenarios) of percent change relative to a stated baseline; no probability is assigned.
Near-term (to mid-century) projections are prioritised because they overlap the strategy horizon; late-century projections are context.
Flow-driven variability and hazard-driven outages are kept as separate channels in the model.

challenges.text: Coordinate on the snow/glacier-fed classification threshold (EXP-07) and on a common basin list and baseline period so 22D and 25A projections are comparable.
Please provide (or confirm availability of) NEA monthly generation by plant and plant type (ROR/PROR/storage); 22D needs it to convert flow projections into generation variability.
units.py has no code for discharge (m3/s) or runoff depth (mm); consider adding if flow observations are to be stored.
Escalation: the August 2026 Kyirong-Rasuwa event (ICIMOD, unverified) may affect generation and export assumptions in S05 and S09.

uncertainty: Very high: nothing retrieved. Projection uncertainty is dominated by precipitation (monsoon) projections, which diverge across climate models in sign as well as magnitude for the Himalaya; melt-driven flow increases are generally considered better constrained than precipitation changes but depend on glacier volume estimates. Conversion to generation adds plant-specific uncertainty and sediment/hazard effects that are not captured by flow projections.
